note: theme_permission replaces core's single 'administer themes' permission with per-theme dynamic permissions generated by ThemePerm::dynamicPermissions() for every installed theme: 'administer themes <theme>', 'uninstall themes <theme>', plus one 'Edit Administration theme'. A RouteSubscriber overrides system.themes_page with AccessController::themesPage (lists only manageable themes) and adds _custom_access (AccessController::access, keyed on the theme query arg) to theme install/uninstall/set-default/settings/block routes. No config form (configure=system.themes_page); permissions are assigned at /admin/people/permissions. On this site the installed themes are olivero and claro, so the machine names include 'administer themes olivero' and 'administer themes claro'. Medium/hard cases use a namespaced role (tp_viewer/tp_task) and read/write those permission strings on the live role config.

evals.prompt: What permissions does the Drupal theme_permission module add, and how are they named for each theme?
evals.expected_output: For every installed theme it generates 'administer themes <theme>' and 'uninstall themes <theme>' (e.g. 'administer themes olivero'), plus a single 'Edit Administration theme' permission. They are produced dynamically by ThemePerm::dynamicPermissions().

evals.prompt: I want to let a role manage only one specific theme on the Appearance page, without giving them core's all-powerful 'administer themes' permission. How does the theme_permission module make that possible?
evals.expected_output: It provides per-theme permissions ('administer themes <theme>'). Grant the role only 'administer themes <thattheme>'; a route subscriber overrides the Appearance page and adds custom access so the user can only see/manage themes they hold the matching permission for.

evals.prompt: Where do you assign the theme_permission per-theme permissions, and does the module have its own configuration page?
evals.expected_output: There is no dedicated config form; its configure route is core's system.themes_page (/admin/appearance). You assign the generated permissions on the normal permissions page at /admin/people/permissions.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a role named tp_viewer that, via the theme_permission module, is allowed to administer exactly one theme. Inspect the live role configuration and state which theme it may administer.
evals.expected_output: Role tp_viewer holds the permission 'administer themes olivero' (inspect user.role.tp_viewer permissions, or Role::load('tp_viewer')->getPermissions()).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a role tp_task. Using the theme_permission module, grant that role permission to administer the Claro theme (and only Claro). Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Grant the theme_permission dynamic permission 'administer themes claro' to role tp_task (e.g. drush role:perm:add tp_task 'administer themes claro', or Role::load('tp_task')->grantPermission('administer themes claro')->save()). Verified against the live role.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a role named tp_uviewer that, via the theme_permission module, is allowed to uninstall exactly one theme. Inspect the live role configuration and state which theme it may uninstall.
evals.expected_output: Role tp_uviewer holds the permission 'uninstall themes claro' (inspect user.role.tp_uviewer permissions, or Role::load('tp_uviewer')->getPermissions()).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a role tp_utask. Using the theme_permission module, grant that role permission to uninstall the Olivero theme. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Grant the theme_permission dynamic permission 'uninstall themes olivero' to role tp_utask (e.g. Role::load('tp_utask')->grantPermission('uninstall themes olivero')->save()). Verified against the live role.
